===Post-Endor===
[[File:X1_Star_DestroyerMustafar.jpg|thumb|left|250px|[[X1]]'s [[X1's Executor-class Star Dreadnought|Star Destroyer]] crashes.]]
Following the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], the death of Emperor Palpatine and Darth Vader the Empire was left shattered. A [[Force-sensitive/Legends|force-sensitive]] [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone trooper]] named [[X1]], who was serving the Empire, used the shattering of the Empire as an opportunity to create his own Empire. As he built up his forces he eventually began calling himself a [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] and constructed a [[X1's Fortress|fortress]] on Mustafar. Determined to stop him, his brother a fellow force-sensitive clone named [[X2]] who left the Empire and worked with the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|rebellion]] and eventually joined [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker's]] new Jedi Order. After [[Battle of Vjun|raiding]] [[Bast Castle]] on [[Vjun/Legends|Vjun]], X1 recovered a [[Holocron/Legends|Hologron]] belonging to X1 which directed them to X1's fortess on Mustafar. Skywalker arrived on Mustafar first and was captured by X1 who planned to use him as a template for an army of [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] clones.<ref name="bfes" />

X2 later arrived at Mustafar with Grey Squadron to [[Battle of Mustafar (Galactic Civil War)|confront X1 and rescue Skywalker]]. After reaching the space above the planet, X2 infiltrated an orbiting Star Destroyer. After sabotaging the Star Destroyer's power reactor and causing it to begin falling to the surface, X1 confronted X2. As the two fought, X1 continued to try to tempt X2 to the dark side. X2 eventually forced X1 to retreat to a [[TIE Advanced x1/Legends|TIE Advanced x1]], X2 pursued in an [[X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing]] and the two resumed their fight in orbit over the planet before X1 retreated to to the planet's surface. X2 regrouped with Grey Squadron on the surface at the wrecked of crashed Star Destroyer. From there they proceeded to an [[Ion cannon/Legends|Ion Cannon]] control room on the surface and deactivate the fortress's ground defenses which allowed a [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|Y-wing starfighter]] to perform a bombing run. After defeating stormtroopers, [[Dark Trooper/Legends|dark troopers]] and [[Hovertank/Legends|hovertanks]] X2 made it into the cloning laboratory where he faced X1 again.<ref name="bfes" />

[[File:X1_lava.jpg|thumb|right|250px|X1 falls to his death.]]
X1 soon dismissed his brother as an unworthy opponent and retreated, but not before releasing his [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookies]] clones to combat X2. After defeating the Wookiee clones, X2 made his way to his brother where he was protected by [[Emperor's Royal Guard/Legends|Royal Guards]]. After another brief fight and defeating the Royal Guards, X2 pursued X1 to a mining platform where they engaged in one final battle.  After being defeated by X2, X1 in a final act, manipulated his dropped lightsaber with the Force to kill X2. X2 jumped over the lightsaber, causing X1 to be impaled by his own blade. With the lightsaber in his chest, X1 stepped back over the edge and fell down into a lava river to his death.<ref name="bfes" />

==Inhabitants==
===Indigenous people===
{{Main|Mustafarian/Legends}}
[[File:Mustafarian_NEGAS.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The two main subspecies of Mustafarian, Southern Mustafarian (left) and Northern Mustafarian (right)]]
Mustafar was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the Mustafarians, a sentient species of arthropod [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]]. Mustafarians were divided into two main [[Subspecies/Legends|subspecies]], the [[Northern Mustafarian/Legends|Northern Mustafarians]] and [[Southern Mustafarian/Legends|Southern Mustafarians]]. The Northern Mustafarians were taller, though weaker, and often served as sentries or security forces and frequently donned mechanical prosthetics to enhance their physical capabilities. The Northern Mustafarians were the subspecies that domesticated and rode the backs of the lava fleas. The Southern Mustafarians were smaller, sturdier, and hardier than their northern counterparts and typically handled the more physical tasks, working in cooperation with their genetic cousins. Because they were more capable of withstanding the higher temperatures, they spent more time on the surface than Northern Mustafarians, wearing armor and [[Breath mask/Legends|breath masks]] to protect themselves from the extreme elements.<ref name="NEGAS" />

The Mustafarians evolved from extremophile arthropods and contained very little water within their biology. Living in cooler hollows of dormant volcanoes, they ventured to the surface following trails left by lava fleas. They established townships that were loosely stitched together through peaceful trade, banding together in the face of extreme conditions. They spoke a clicking, [[Insectoid/Legends|insectiod]] [[Mustafarian (language)/Legends|language]], and as a result of their skin being resistant to the heat of most [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]], they armed themselves with a type of native blaster that emitted bolts of kinetic force. The indigenous people of Mustafar paid little attention to the concerns of offworlders, choosing instead to focus on harvesting the minerals found within their homeworld's lava flows.<ref name="DB Mustafarian" />

===Religious seekers===
[[File:Blackguard-SWGTCGAoD.jpg|thumb|right|270px|A member of the Blackguard dark side cult that existed on Mustafar for around a millennium.]]
Around 5300 BBY, a Jedi enclave was constructed on Mustafar and became home to Jedi Master Chu-Don Gar. After an attack by the Sith in 3996 BBY that resulted in Lefrani being pulled closer to Jestefad, originating the tidal stresses that constantly pulled Mustafar apart, all surface life on Mustafar was destroyed.<ref name="TEA" /> Following a search for Force-related artifacts after the [[Seventh Battle of Ruusan|Battle of Ruusan]]<ref name="JATM">''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]''</ref> in [[1000 BBY]],<ref name="TEA" /> [[Vulta Daanat]] learned many secrets of the dark side and settled in the [[Southern Jedi Ruins]] on Mustafar, taking on several apprentices to pass on his knowledge to a new generation. The group became the [[Blackguard (Mustafar)/Legends|Blackguard]] and fluctuated in size from mammoth proportions to a mere handful. Eventually, the cult came under the control of [[San'sii]] the Kursk, who began the practice of recruiting non-Force-sensitives to help the cult survive.<ref name="JATM" /> He, along with many members of the Blackguard, was killed<ref name="SWG:AAP" /> in [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]].<ref name="SWG_timeline" /> By approximately [[138 ABY]],<ref name="extremes">''[[Star Wars: Legacy Volume 10: Extremes]]''</ref> the Sith of [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire]] had a presence on Mustafar.<ref name="Legacy50" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|It was a whole part of the plot that essentially got cut out. It may be in one of the sequels. ''[…]'' Ben and Vader have a confrontation, just like they have in ''Star Wars'', and Ben almost kills Vader. As a matter of fact, he falls into a volcanic pit and gets fried and is one destroyed being.|George Lucas on August 25, 1977, the earliest known mention of what would become Mustafar|<ref name="Rolling Stone">{{WebCite|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/movies/movie-news/george-lucas-the-wizard-of-star-wars-2-232011|text=George Lucas: The Wizard of 'Star Wars'|author=Scanlon, Paul|date=1977-08-25|archivedate=20200623204338}}</ref>}}
Mustafar, originally known as "Mufasta" in early drafts<ref name="db" /> made its first appearance in the [[2005]] film [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Revenge of the Sith'']].<ref name="RotS" /> However the planet and Vader's injuries there were alluded to since [[August 25]], [[1977]], when in an interview published by ''Rolling Stone'', [[George Lucas]] said that Vader fell into a volcanic pit while dueling Obi-Wan and that the resulting injuries are why he wears [[Darth Vader's armor/Legends|his armor]].<ref name="Rolling Stone" /> Lucas also mentioned this backstory to [[Lawrence Kasdan]] during the writing of [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']]<ref name="Making of">''[[The Making of Return of the Jedi]]''</ref> and this backstory is mentioned in the [[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|novelization]] of ''Return of the Jedi''.<ref name="ROJN">[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Star Wars: Return of the Jedi'' novelization]]</ref> The concept of a lava duel also appears in the [[Star Wars: Episode VI Revenge of the Jedi|Rough Draft]] and Revised Rough Draft of the script for ''Return of the Jedi'', in which Luke Skywalker battles Darth Vader over a lava lake in Palpatine's throne room in the lowest levels of the [[Imperial Palace/Legends|Imperial Palace]].<ref name="Making of" />

[[File:SWCL_Mustafar.jpg|thumb|right|220px|The [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] headquarters, as illustrated in [[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']].]]

[[Mount Etna]] was scouted for [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Revenge of the Sith'']], to capture plate photography for backdrops in the [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] vs. [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] fight on Mustafar. Conveniently, Etna erupted during the making of the film, so Lucas sent a team which included [[Rick McCallum]] and [[Ron Fricke]] to film it. The resultant moving image of lava flows could be used as backgrounds for the duel.<ref name="db" /> These images could have been done by CGI, in theory, but it would have been more difficult and expensive than sending a few people to Sicily with cameras, as [[George Lucas|Lucas]] states in the audio commentary to Episode III.

The film relied heavily on blue and green screens when filming scenes on Mustafar however the final lava river bank was practically built and included a dyed methylcyl which was lit from below to simulate the stage lava. The scenes utilized red lighting, wind and smoke machines extensively during filming. In post production, the [[Industrial Light & Magic]] team used digital models including digital lava that would flow and burst realistically to composite with the scenes.<ref name="db" /> Several versions of the scene where Padmé and Anakin meet on Mustafar were filmed, in at least one the two shared a kiss but ultimately it was cut along with a story angle involving Anakin developing jealousy of Obi-Wan.<ref name="Ask Lobot">{{InsiderCite|106|Ask Lobot}}</ref>

In [[2010]], [[Abrams Books]] published ''[[Star Wars Art: Visions]]'' which featured artwork from 100 different artists set in the ''Star Wars'' franchise. Two pieces depicted Anakin standing on the surface of Mustafar; ''Portrait of Darth Vader'' by [[Steven J. Levin]] and ''Anakin Skywalker'' by [[Richard Piloco]].<ref name="Art Visions">''[[Star Wars Art: Visions]]''</ref>

===Non-canonical appearances===
{{Quote|I came a across a corpse on Mustafar I thought might've been you. Imagine my relief.|Darth Maul, to Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="Old Wounds">{{StoryCite|story=Old Wounds|book=Star Wars: Visionaries}}</ref>}}
In "[[Old Wounds]]", a short non-[[canon]] comic written and illustrated by [[Aaron McBride]], and published in ''[[Star Wars: Visionaries]]'' by [[Dark Horse Comics]] on [[April 2]], 2005, Mustafar makes a brief appearance as one of locations where Darth Maul searches for Obi-Wan Kenobi after surviving his [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|injuries]] on [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. Maul encountered a wounded Anakin Skywalker on Mustafar and was relieved to realize that he was not Kenobi, before following the Jedi's trail to Polis Massa. Maul later recounted his journey after tracking the Jedi down to the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="Old Wounds" />
